Sara: hey folks :wave: I'm Sara (started this week). Trying to open my first PR against repo `runtime` but hit a few questions — branch naming, small PR vs batch, and flaky CI failures. Who should I ping for a quick walkthrough?
Olivia: welcome Sara! For branches we usually do `feat/<initials>/<short-desc>` for features, `fix/<initials>/<short-desc>` for bugfixes. e.g. `feat/sa/add-prefix-cache`.
Mira: +1. Also keep PRs small when possible — target <200 LOC. If it's unavoidably bigger, split into logical commits and explain the rollout plan in the PR body.
Sara: thanks — good to know about the size. about CI: my build failed on `integration-e2e` but unit and lint passed. flaky?
Sam: ping me the link and I can take a look. A lot of the e2e flakes are timing-related on long sequences; locally run `./scripts/e2e --focus=your-test` to reproduce quickly.
Olivia: and before opening, run pre-commit hooks: `pre-commit run --all-files`. Our common checklist is in the PR template — copy+pasted below.
Mira: PR template snippet:```
- What changed and why (1-2 sentences)
- How to validate locally (commands)
- Rollout plan / revert steps
- Tests added or manual steps verified
- CI status: all green (or known flakes documented)
```
Sara: could someone pair with me for the first PR review? I want to learn the code layout and reviewers' expectations. 30 min would help.
Sam: I can do 30m at 16:00 PT today. I'll review the code and walkthrough the runtime hot paths.
Olivia: If Sam is busy, @Mira can handle the API/contract bits. Also drop the PR link here and mention area owners in the description: `area: runtime-cache` etc.
Mira: small tip — include `slo: none` label if this is experimental, and add `breaking-change: no` unless you're changing public API.
devex-bot: CI build started for branch feat/sa/add-prefix-cache (job #4821) :gear:
